name: Mattithiah
overview: Mattithiah was a male Levite who played a significant role during the public reading of the Law in Nehemiah 8:4. He is notably recognized for standing at Ezra's right hand as the Law was read, indicating a position of honor and responsibility. His Levite status is inferred from this event, reflecting his service in the religious life of Israel.
namesAndTitles: The name Mattithiah means 'gift of YHWH,' highlighting a meaningful theophoric element common in Hebrew names. This proper name, as recorded in Nehemiah 8:4, emphasizes God's gracious provision and blessing, though it was not given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Mattithiah as a descendant of Levi, which aligns with his role in the religious service. Beyond this tribal affiliation, no further family relationships are recorded in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Mattithiah's presence at Ezra's right hand during the reading of the Law underscores his important role in the spiritual renewal of Israel after the exile. As a Levite, he would have been entrusted with duties related to the teaching and preservation of God's Word. His position reflects the reverence and orderliness with which the Law was restored and taught to the people, marking a pivotal moment in Israel's return to covenant faithfulness.
